notes: rust_stdlib::text::scanner: Go's tokenizer ported literally (same buffers, read sizes, error texts and positions), over std::io::Read. Token text is returned as bytes because Go strings may hold invalid UTF-8. tests/text_scanner.rs ports scanner_test.go (tables generated from the Go source); tools/text_scanner_check.py compares tokens, positions, error callbacks, Peek/Next and Read-call counts with Go over 6000 vectors. Error messages written to standard error without a callback are not compared.

Position.String.note: Position implements Display; the text is Go's filename:line:column with <input> for an empty filename.

Scanner.note: Go's zero value is Scanner::default(); the reader is a Box<dyn Read> and the error callback an Rc<dyn Fn>, so a callback may clear or replace Scanner::error while it runs, as in Go.

Scanner.Init.note: std::io::Read cannot return data together with an error, so a read error delivers no bytes (Go delivers the bytes of a (n, err) read first); and Ok(0) is end of source, where Go's (0, nil) asks for another read. Both are the Read contract, and the scanner reports read errors through Scanner::error as Go does.

Scanner.TokenText.note: Returns the token's bytes (Vec<u8>), not a string, so invalid UTF-8 is preserved.
